rationale: This record is a broad narrative book chapter surveying water and wastewater technologies (membrane filtration, desalination, AI, IoT and rainwater harvesting) alongside general macro-governance and policy themes across developed and developing countries. It reports no primary empirical research or systematic review methodology (failing Criterion 3, E05) and examines no specific legal or administrative rule-type mechanism governing household or community service access (failing narrow Criterion 2).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the plain Criterion 2 wording, general discussion of regulatory frameworks, strong institutions, enforcement and policy reform touches institutional and governance factors, whereas under the narrow reading these appear only as unanalysed macro-governance background alongside treatment technologies. Both decisions remain exclude because the chapter presents a non-empirical narrative overview rather than primary empirical evidence or a systematic review (E05).

evidence_quotes.quote: Water and wastewater applications in developed and developing countries: extant experience and plan for the future
This chapter highlights the significance of innovation, policy reform, and international cooperation in bridging the gap between developing and developed nations.
Governance and policy frameworks significantly impact water management, with strong institutions and enforcement ensuring sustainability in developed nations.
